Subject: GPU runway readiness: Galileo (late-stage)

Rishi,

Quick ask — Galileo is pushing to close GA-2047 next week. Sales asked for a "runway" check to understand if we can guarantee a soft allocation (+ burst) matching their forecast for Q4 ramp. They want to see an internal availability statement we can share with Procurement and legal for SOW sizing.

Topline ask: can you confirm whether we have a 30-60-90 day allocation profile (per-customer reserved GPU vram/TU) we can offer as a provisional hold for this deal? If not, what is the minimal commitment we need to reserve to meet their latency SLOs?

I've attached the Galileo forecast we received (galileo_map_v2.xlsx). No need to lock anything yet — this is a probe to prep the demo with them and to surface any risk.

Thanks — appreciate a quick sanity check.

—Karthik
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Karthik — thanks for the context. Looping in Soojin (capacity planning) and Marcus (infrastructure ops) to get a real runway snapshot and a recommended soft-hold play.

Action items for Soojin/Marcus:
- Can we produce the 30/60/90-day availability table aligned to Galileo's forecast (per-tenant reserved vram + burst headroom)?
- Flag any region restrictions (they prefer us-west).

Karthik — if we can produce this by EOD Friday (7/16) we can share a one-page internal readiness note with Procurement at Galileo before their legal review.

--Rishi

Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-07-14T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GPU runway readiness: Galileo (late-stage)

Rishi / Karthik — attaching a preliminary snapshot (gpu_runway_snapshot.pdf). Summary below.

Summary (preliminary):
- Current free pool (us-west): 28 A100-equivalent units available for soft allocation in the next 30 days; additional 42 available via burst (no guaranteed commit) but would increase latency risk at 95th percentile if used heavily.
- 60-day view: without adjustments, soft-allocatable units drop to ~18 due to scheduled cluster maintenance and several committed launches.
- 90-day: projection shows pressure at peak windows (evenings PST) unless we apply a conservative per-deal cap or shift some traffic to our europe/asia pools (they indicated preference for us-west).

Recommendation:
1) Offer Galileo a provisional soft-hold of 12 A100-equivalent reserved units for the first 60 days with the option to scale +8 for burst (total 20) under a 24-hour advance notice; label this internally as "soft-provisional hold — non-binding".
2) If they need a contract-backed guarantee, require a 6-month minimum for 12 units (or a usage-based SLA uplift).

Notes: the numbers above assume standard quantization profiles; custom quantization or longer context windows will change effective capacity. See attached snapshot and a short runbook.

Attachment: gpu_runway_snapshot.pdf (PDF, 210 KB)

—Soojin
Capacity Planning Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-07-15T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GPU runway readiness: Galileo (late-stage)

Soojin — appreciate the snapshot. Couple of infra constraints to call out before we present anything externally:

- Maintenance window: a planned kernel upgrade across two us-west racks is scheduled on 2029-07-28 -> reduces usable capacity by ~6 units for 48 hours. We can shift some workloads to other racks but that requires coordination and a temporary routing policy change.
- Model variant compatibility: Galileo's default model uses long-context settings that increase KV cache usage; if they keep those settings, their per-token cost is ~1.25x and effective capacity reduces accordingly.
- Network: Hyperscale partner is doing a fabric upgrade in week 31; we should not promise headroom reliant solely on their burst pool.

Operational recommendation:
- Approve Soojin's provisional soft-hold (12 reserved + 8 burst) but mark it with an operational exception: "subject to scheduled infra events; guaranteed backup routing to eu-central required for critical windows."
- Start a quick runbook for the account: escalation path, change windows, and a short list of required latency benchmarks to include in the internal readiness note.

I'll prepare the runbook skeleton once we agree on the provisional numbers.

—Marcus
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: GPU runway readiness: Galileo (late-stage)

All — thanks, this is helpful and pragmatic. Kicking the sales side: authorize the provisional soft-hold as recommended (12 reserved + 8 burst) and we will include the operational exception language in external communications.

Karthik -> Alex / Procurement: we will send an internal readiness memo tomorrow that outlines the provisional hold, the operational exception, and the ask for a 6-month minimum if they want contract-backed guarantees.

Rishi: please push the one-pager into HubSpot (linked) and flag a DocuSign SOW template if they push for contract-backed reserve.

—Karthik

- Karthik: share the readiness note with Alex/Procurement tomorrow and request confirmation on runway acceptance or ask for contract-backed commit.

Rishi
